h1: Melanotan II ('tanning injections', the Barbie drug): what four small trials found, why it was abandoned, and what the case reports and vials show
dek: A cyclic α-MSH analogue from Arizona that tans skin, causes erections and nausea, and was never developed past a handful of men in the 1990s; its metabolite became the approved libido drug PT-141 and its linear cousin the approved orphan drug Scenesse. This page tables the trials with their doses, the harm reports since, and what the analysed vials actually contained.

Does melanotan II cause melanoma?
queries.answer: Unproven and not ruled out. Case reports describe melanomas diagnosed in users, a 2025 report describes a mucosal melanoma in the mouth of a 22-year-old after nasal use, and the drug reliably darkens and enlarges moles, which can hide or mimic melanoma. Most reported users also used sunbeds. No study has followed users long enough to measure risk in either direction; the melanocortin-1 receptor melanotan II activates is the receptor that governs pigment, and melanocytes are the cells melanoma comes from.

queries.heading: What is melanotan II?
queries.answer: Melanotan II is a synthetic cyclic peptide copied from the active core of the pigment hormone α-MSH, made at the University of Arizona in the late 1980s as a possible sunless tanning agent to prevent skin cancer. It activates several melanocortin receptors at once: MC1R in skin, which darkens pigment, and MC3 and MC4 in the brain, which produce erections, nausea, yawning and appetite loss. It was tested in a handful of men in the 1990s, never developed further, and is now sold illegally online as the 'Barbie drug' for tanning.

queries.heading: What is the half-life of melanotan II?
queries.answer: Not stated in any abstract in the ledger. The erection trials monitored effects for six hours after a subcutaneous dose, and the phase 1 pilot reported spontaneous erections for one to five hours after dosing; a 1994 preformulation study measured 4.6 percent oral bioavailability in rats. The tan itself persists for weeks because it is melanin in the skin, not the drug in the blood, which is why users move to weekly maintenance.

queries.heading: Is melanotan II hard on the kidneys?
queries.answer: No trial measured kidney function, and no case report in the ledger describes kidney injury. Vendor pages mention rhabdomyolysis at overdose, which would strain the kidneys; that claim comes from case reports not in this record and is unverified here. What the trials did record was nausea, yawning, erections and sleepiness at the top dose.

queries.heading: Does melanotan II burn fat?
queries.answer: In mice and rats, yes: melanotan II activates the MC4 receptor that suppresses appetite, and chronic infusion reduced food intake and body fat in several rodent studies in the ledger. In people the trials recorded decreased appetite as a side effect and measured nothing about weight; no human study has tested it for fat loss, and its effects on heart rate and blood pressure in rodents are the reason MC4 agonists for obesity have been hard to develop.

queries.heading: Can melanotan II change eye colour?
queries.answer: No study has reported it, and the biology runs the other way: melanotan II stimulates melanin production, which darkens, not lightens. Forum reports of eye changes exist; the ledger has none, and a pigment-stimulating drug acting on the iris would be a reason for concern rather than a feature.

information_gain: The only page that tables melanotan II's entire human trial record, four studies in 3 to 20 men at 0.01 to 0.03 mg/kg by the group that invented it, with nausea, yawning and erection rates, and shows the tanning trial that everyone assumes exists was never run; that traces both approved descendants (bremelanotide, its metabolite, for libido; afamelanotide, the linear analogue, for erythropoietic protoporphyria) and explains why the parent was dropped; that reports the 2015 analysis of online vials (4 to 9 mg per vial, impurities to 5.9 percent), the 2021 forum study of 623 entries, and the 2025 and 2026 case reports of oral mucosal melanoma after nasal use, gingival pigmentation and surgical priapism; and that states the legal position in the UK, US and Australia rather than 'research use only'.
